{"status":"available","text":"LoopVL 考察的核心问题是：能否把 Loop Transformers 有效扩展到 vision–language models（E025）。它的输入是一条包含 conditioning header、image、instruction 与 response 的序列：image 部分由 frozen 的 Penguin Vision Encoder 对每个保留的 image patch 产生 1024 维特征，再由两层 GELU projector 经 1536 维隐层把特征映射到 1536 维，投影后的 embedding 替换序列中预留的 visual slots（E040）。最终输出由 language-modeling head 产生，模型据此给出答案。

语言骨干建立在 HRM-Text 的开源框架之上，包含互不共享参数的 L 与 H 两个参数栈，每栈 16 层 Transformer，各自在被反复调用时复用自身参数（E041）。默认 H2L3 配置的执行顺序是 L→L→L→H→L→L→L→H（E042）。这里的 L 或 H 记号代表一次完整模块调用而非单个 attention 层，因此骨干虽只存两套 16 层堆叠，一次完整前向却执行 128 次 Transformer 层调用（E044）。模块内部由 normalization、gated self-attention、residual 路径与 SwiGLU feed-forward 组成（E045）。visual tokens 使用二维 spatial RoPE，以图像网格上的行、列坐标编码空间位置；text tokens 也被赋予二维坐标，但两个坐标沿文本序列同步推进，从而退化为与原来一维 RoPE 等价的效果（E045）。attention 计算内部施加 PrefixLM mask，attention 子层中的 gate 调制其输出路径，这些操作在模块再次被调用时复用（E047）。

状态更新上，recurrent computation 维护耦合的 L 与 H 状态：H 状态由缩放后的 input embedding 初始化，L 状态初始化为零并在 model cycles 之间保留（E048）。每个 cycle 内，L 在当前高层条件下被反复更新，随后 H 更新并纳入细化后的 L 状态，最终 H 状态送入 language-modeling head；这不同于堆叠一串独立 block，共享的 L 变换会在 H 更新下一个 cycle 的条件之前被多次重访。每个 model cycle 开始时，LoopVL 会把来自初始投影视觉 embedding 的固定 anchor 重新注入 H 状态的 visual positions，注入强度由 query-conditioned 的 token-wise visual gate 与可学习的 cycle-specific scale 控制（E048）。由此，Module-Loop 在同一高层条件下提供更密集的状态更新，Model-Loop 让整合后的高层状态再次参与后续计算，两者构成快慢两种时间尺度的嵌套更新（E053），默认调度为 [L × 3 → H] × 2（E036）。

训练时的反向传播采用 selective backpropagation：默认 H2L3 下的执行顺序为 L1→L2→L3→H1→L4→L5→L6→H2，warmup 期间 active backward graph 从最后两次调用（L6、H2）逐步扩展到最后五次（L4、L5、L6、H1、H2），较早的 L1–L3 不参与梯度计算，但所有 recurrent invocation 仍在前向中执行（E049）。所有 valid sequence positions 都参与模块调用，区别只在 attention 可见性：header、image、instruction 共同构成双向 prefix，response 位置可关注该 prefix 及其之前的 response 位置，而 prefix 位置不能关注 response（E049）。

整体训练流程分语言预训练与多模态两阶段。语言预训练沿用 HRM-Text 公开数据配方并加入自整理数据，共 75B tokens，其中 60B 来自 HRM-Text base、15B 为整理数据（E088）。Stage 1: Visual Language Alignment 冻结 language backbone 与 Penguin Vision Encoder，只训练 visual interface（E104）；该阶段使用 LLaVA-559K WebDataset、0.33B tokens、最大序列长度 2048、每图 256–1024 visual tokens，以 image–caption 监督并把 loss 落在 response tokens 上（E118）。Stage 2: Multimodal Mid-Training 改为联合更新 language model 与 visual interface，Penguin 仍冻结（E121）；此阶段最大序列长度 3072、global batch size 128、visual token 范围仍为 256–1024（E123），使用 OneVision-1.5 Mid-Training-85M 的 49B tokens 并维持 response-only 训练目标（E124）。初始化时视觉编码器保留 Penguin 预训练权重，language backbone 使用自训文本预训练的 H2L3 checkpoint，projector 随机初始化并在 Stage 1 训练，且不加载此前的 optimizer、scheduler 与 trainer 状态（E106）。视觉接口先对视觉特征做无参数 RMS 归一化，再校准到 language embedding 向量的中位 RMS，Penguin 与 language backbone 用 BF16，projector 参数保持 FP32（E107）。优化使用 AdamW，(β1,β2)=(0.9,0.95)，gradient-norm clipping 为 1.0，warmup 覆盖总训练步数的 3%（E109）；Stage 1 的 projector 学习率为 10^-3、Stage 2 的 language backbone 学习率为 2×10^-5（E112），Stage 2 的 projector 用 10^-4，weight decay 为 0（E114）；两阶段 global batch size 分别为 256 与 128，Stage 2 在 warmup 后使用 cosine 学习率衰减（E115）。

后训练阶段先用 supervised fine-tuning，仍使用 PrefixLM mask：image 与 instruction 组成双向 conditioning prefix，response 位置可关注该 prefix 及之前的 response tokens（E142）。条件生成概率分解为 p_θ(y∣x)=∏_{t=1}^{T} p_θ(y_t∣x, y_<t)（E144），训练以 teacher forcing 最小化一个 batch 内有效 response tokens 上的平均交叉熵，并屏蔽 padding 位置（E146）。SFT 共使用 16.81B tokens（E140）。随后进行 visual reinforcement learning，采用 GRPO 并组合答案正确性奖励与 progressive reasoning-length schedule（E156）：对每个 image–question 输入采样一组 responses，最终答案与参考答案一致给正奖励、否则为零，GRPO 由 group-normalized rewards 计算 advantage，并用 probability-ratio clipping 与对 reference policy 的 KL 正则更新策略（E157）；生成上限从 2048 逐步增加到 4096 tokens，并在上限提高时减少每个输入的候选数（E158）。

评测使用统一推理与打分流程，VLMEvalKit 为部分 benchmark 提供数据加载与 prompt 构建，主要采用 direct-answer prompts、greedy decoding、batch size 1、随机种子 0，多数样本生成预算为 32 tokens（部分为 8、64 或 512），预测通过 option extraction、answer normalization 与任务特定匹配规则打分（E208）。主模型使用 H2L3、每次前向 128 次层执行；H/L sweep 在同一 checkpoint 上遍历 H 取 1–4、L 取 1–3 共 12 种配置，H 状态由多模态 input embeddings 初始化、L 状态使用 checkpoint 中保存的初始状态，decoding 关闭 KV cache，最终 H-module 输出经共享 output head 生成答案（E210）。","sources":["E025","E040","E041","E042","E044","E045","E047","E048","E053","E036","E049","E088","E104","E118","E121","E123","E124","E106","E107","E109","E112","E114","E115","E142","E144","E146","E140","E156","E157","E158","E208","E210"]}

Key method elements:

Task/question: Can Loop Transformers be effectively extended to vision–language models? (E025)

Architecture (E040): LoopVL uses Penguin Vision Encoder as frozen visual encoder, trainable visual interface, and own pretrained recurrent language backbone. Language backbone built upon HRM-Text's open-source framework. Pretraining data based on publicly released HRM-Text training data, augmented with additional curated data. Penguin Vision Encoder produces 1024-dim feature for each retained image patch. Two-layer GELU projector maps each visual feature from 1024 to 1536 dims through a 1536-dim hidden layer. Projected embeddings replace reserved visual slots in sequence containing conditioning header, image, instruction, response.

Language backbone: separate L and H parameter stacks, each 16 Transformer layers (E041). Each stack shares its own parameters across repeated invocations; L and H don't share with each other. Default H2L3 config execution order: L→L→L→H→L→L→L→H (E041, E042).

An L or H symbol denotes complete module invocation not individual attention layer; backbone stores only two 16-layer stacks but complete forward execution performs 128 Transformer-layer calls (E044).

Within each module: normalization, gated self-attention, residual paths, SwiGLU feed-forward (E045). Visual and text tokens use different RoPE: visual tokens use two-dimensional spatial RoPE with row/column coordinates on image grid; text tokens also assigned two-dimensional coordinates but advance synchronously reducing to equivalent of original 1D RoPE (E045). PrefixLM mask applied within attention; gate inside attention sublayer modulates output path; operations reused on each invocation (E047).

Recurrent computation maintains coupled L and H states (E048). H state initialized from scaled input embeddings, L state initialized to zero and retained across model cycles. Within each cycle, L repeatedly updated under current high-level condition, followed by H update incorporating refined L state. Final H state passed to LM head. Differs from stacking independent blocks. At start of each model cycle, LoopVL re-injects a fixed anchor from initial projected visual embeddings into visual positions of H state. A query-conditioned token-wise visual gate and learnable cycle-specific scale control strength of re-injection (E048).

Training: selective backpropagation across recurrent invocations (E049). For default H2L3 schedule, order L1→L2→L3→H1→L4→L5→L6→H2. During backprop warmup, active backward graph expands from final two invocations (L6, H2) to final five (L4, L5, L6, H1, H2). Earlier L calls (L1,L2,L3) excluded from gradient computation. All recurrent invocations executed in forward pass. All valid sequence positions participate in module invocations, but attention visibility differs: header, image, instruction positions form bidirectional prefix; response positions attend to prefix and preceding response positions; prefix cannot attend to response (E049).

Motivation: Module-Loop provides denser state updates under same high-level condition, Model-Loop allows integrated high-level state to participate again (E053). Default schedule [L×3→H]×2 (E036).

"3 Why Need Loop?" comparison (E055-E068): LoopVL vs three non-recurrent Transformer-VL baselines at 0.14T token budget. Transformer-VL 1B: 32 layers, hidden 1536, matching LoopVL unique layers and hidden. Transformer-VL 4B (Deep): 78 layers, hidden 1792. Transformer-VL 4B (Wide): 32 layers, hidden 2816. Results in Table 1.

"2.4 Why Loop Visual Tokens?" (E069-E085): visual tokens evolve. Controls: Normal, Block L visual updates, Freeze visual states, Read-only trained (E073, E083, E084). Retrained variant preserves H2L3 schedule, both 16-layer shared stacks, final H-state readout; at first-cycle boundary saves separate L/H visual-state references; during second cycle persistent visual states restored to references after writeback; within each module, visual residual states restored after every attention and feed-forward update to reference taken from that invocation's normally combined input. Visual tokens remain readable and nonvisual states continue updating. Restriction adds no loss or extra visual-encoder pass and doesn't freeze second-cycle model parameters (E085).

Training pipeline: 
- Text pretraining based on HRM-Text's open-source framework, 75B tokens (60B HRM-Text base + 15B curated) (E088).
- Stage 1: Visual Language Alignment — freeze language backbone and Penguin Vision Encoder, train only visual interface (E104). LLaVA-559K WebDataset, 0.33B tokens, max seq len 2048, 256–1024 visual tokens per image, image-caption supervision with loss on response tokens (E118). Retained input-gradient path enables recurrent language backbone to propagate learning signals to visual interface (E119).
- Stage 2: Multimodal Mid-Training — jointly update LM and visual interface, keep Penguin frozen (E104). Max seq len 3072, global batch 128, visual tokens 256–1024 (E123). OneVision-1.5 Mid-Training-85M, full 49B-token allocation (E124). Response-only training objective. Data conversion: preserve original ground-truth responses, instruction rewriting for task phrasing normalization, OCR/document retain original wording, multiple-choice standardized to option letter + answer text, yes/no short responses, image hashes and normalized question text for dedup (E125). Long-response filtering removes samples rather than truncating (E126).

Initialization (E105-E107): visual encoder retains Penguin pretrained init; language backbone uses H2L3 checkpoint from own text pretraining. In dynamic-resolution Stage 1 config, projector randomly initialized and trained during Stage 1. Previous optimizer, scheduler, trainer states not loaded. At visual interface, parameter-free RMS normalization applied to visual features, then calibration to median RMS of language embedding vectors. Visual representations then follow standard backbone path with inherited embedding scaling. Penguin and language backbone use BF16, projector in FP32. Regression tests before multimodal training verify text-position compatibility, visual-slot counts, loss masks, frozen/trainable boundaries.

Learning schedule (E108-E116): AdamW with (β1,β2)=(0.9,0.95), gradient-norm clipping 1.0, LR warmup 3% of total steps. Stage 1 projector LR 10^-3. Stage 2 language backbone LR 2×10^-5, projector 10^-4. Weight decay 0. Global batch sizes 256 (Stage 1) and 128 (Stage 2). Gradient checkpointing enabled, inference caching disabled. Stage 2 cosine decay after warmup. Active backward graph follows selective recurrent schedule. Length bucketing and batch-local padding. Causal cross-entropy loss only on valid response tokens, prefix and padding masked.

Post-training (E135-E158): SFT with 16.81B tokens from four sources (OneVision-1.5 Instruct-22M 13B, OneVision Spatial-4M 3B, LLaVA v1.5 Mix665K 0.55B, Vision-R1-Cold 0.26B) (E140). PrefixLM mask, image+instruction form bidirectional prefix, response positions attend to prefix and preceding response tokens (E142). Conditional generation factorized p_θ(y|x)=∏ p_θ(y_t|x,y_<t) (E144). Teacher forcing, mean cross-entropy over valid response tokens masking padding (E146-E154).

RL: GRPO for visual reinforcement learning, answer-correctness reward + progressive reasoning-length schedule (E156). Group sampling, positive rewards when final answers match, GRPO computes advantages from group-normalized rewards, updates policy with probability-ratio clipping and KL regularization against reference policy (E157). Progressive Thinking Suppression Training, increasing max generation length from 2048 to 4096 tokens (E158).

Evaluation settings (E208-E210): unified inference and scoring pipeline, VLMEvalKit for subset. Direct-answer prompts, greedy decoding, batch size 1, seed 0, generation budget 32 tokens for most, fixed budgets 8/64/512 for selected. Scored via option extraction, answer normalization, task-specific matching. Main model H2L3, 128 layer executions per forward pass. H/L sweep over 12 configurations, H 1-4, L 1-3. H state initialized from multimodal input embeddings, L state uses initial state stored in checkpoint. Decoding with KV cache disabled, final H-module output through shared output head. All sweep configs use 32-token budget.

Diagnostics (E212-E214): attention curves use 32 examples, four VQA task families, 8 each. Spatial entropy and coverage from reference-answer queries, averaged over queries, 12 heads, examples. Coverage: fraction of visual tokens for 80% attention mass. Gini aggregates instruction and reference-answer queries per head. State and output probes use 16 VMCBench + 16 AI2D examples. Visual L2 update measures representation changes across complete 16-layer module invocation. Logit lens applies final normalization of corresponding stack and shared output head. Attention indices 0-127, state/output probes cumulative layer-execution counts 1-128.
